correctness.rationale: For a finite subsemigroup T of B_m(G), if ambient zero is absent, squaring forces every element into one diagonal group. With ambient zero, every nonzero diagonal image lies in an abelian group K_i and different diagonal positions meet only at the absorbing zero; any off-diagonal image annihilates all commuting quotient images, including the opposite-index case where c^2=z inside a diagonal image group. Every listed disjoint union embeds using t diagonal positions and, when annihilator X is present, two fresh endpoints (a,b) with distinct group labels. The lower bound follows from distinct nonzero diagonal idempotents and an off-diagonal square-zero image whose endpoints cannot overlap them. Singleton and group cases give b=1. Inspected CHECK.py exhaustively enumerates subsemigroups/congruences of five-element trivial-group Brandt and explicit embeddings; this code is corroboration only.
